title: Telemetry Signal Playbook — Fallback & Degraded Modes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for which telemetry signals we need to capture, how to instrument traces, and what dashboards/alerts to compose for degraded and fallback inference modes. Focus is on actionable observability that helps engineering quickly identify root cause and select an appropriate mitigation (roll back, route, or scale).

Scope:
- Services: inference-gateway, kv-cache, batching-worker, model-host
- Modes: graceful degradation (quantized fallbacks, lower token budget), full fallback (hosted->dedicated, or different model family), network/region failover
- Audience: SREs, runtime engineers, oncall, solutions eng

High-level goals / success criteria (what good looks like):
- Mean time to targeted mitigation <= 10 minutes for common fallback scenarios
- Dashboards surface a single prioritized hypothesis with 3 supporting signals (latency, error-rate by code, and model-quality regression)
- Traces include a low-overhead anchor that survives sampling for causal linkage across components

Signal taxonomy (quick):
- Availability: 4xx/5xx counts, per-route and per-model variant
- Latency slices: p50/p95/p99 by route, by seq-length bucket, by model-variant
- Resource saturation: GPU mem util, host GPU queue depth, host process runq length (sampled)
- Degradation indicators: kv-cache hit ratio (prefix-based), batching rate (requests/sec -> tokens/sec), evicted-kv-count
- Quality/regression: sampled output hash mismatch against canary prompt set, eval-score-drop (rolling window)
- Routing events: policy-fallbacks (count of requests routed to fallback path), region_fallback_count

Minimal metric definitions (for instrumentation):
- inference.request.count: tags={route, customer_tier, model_variant, region} value=increment
- inference.request.latency_ms: tags same as above value=histogram (buckets: 5,10,25,50,100,200,500,1000,2000)
- inference.request.error_code: tags={code,route,model_variant} value=increment
- kv_cache.lookup: tags={route,prefix_length,hit_or_miss} value=increment
- kv_cache.evictions: tags={cache_shard} value=increment
- batching.batch_size: tags={worker_pool} value=gauge (running average per minute)
- model.host.queue_depth: tags={host_id,model_variant} value=gauge
- telemetry.fallback.trigger: tags={from_variant,to_variant,reason} value=increment

Tracing anchors & span guidance (low overhead):
- Root span (gateway) should contain: request_id, route, model_variant_hint, seq_len, sampling_hint (0/1)
- Insert a small “fallback-decision” span at the policy layer with tags: decision, reason_code, fallback_target
- Key KV cache spans should be lightweight: name=kv.lookup shard=%s hit=true/false duration_ms
- Sampling strategy: always capture 1 in 200 requests globally, but 1 in 10 for requests that hit any fallback trigger (policy or error). Ensure sampled traces for high-severity alerts are kept (use_trace_keep flag).

Dashboard ideas (widgets and intent):
1) Fallback Overview (single row):
   - Small heatmap: fallback_trigger_rate by route x region (last 1h)
   - Sparkline: requests routed to primary model vs fallback (ratio)
   - Alert status indicator (if > threshold)
   Intent: triage where fallbacks are spiking and whether it's global or regional.

2) Latency & Resource Correlation panel:
   - p95 latency by model_variant stacked with GPU queue depth (shared Y-axis)
   - Scatter: batch_size vs lat_p95 colored by worker_pool
   Intent: spot batching degenerations or overloaded hosts causing latency spikes that precede fallback.

3) Quality Regression inspector:
   - Rolling eval-score for canary prompts with anomaly shading
   - Sampled recent responses (5) where eval-score dropped fastest with links to trace/request_id
   Intent: determine if fallback was due to quality regressions (bad weights) vs infra failure.

4) KV cache health snapshot:
   - Hit ratio over time by prefix_length bucket
   - Evictions per shard (bar) with latency tail for cache misses
   Intent: detect cache thrash causing increased token generation cost and latency.

Alerting recommendations (practical):
- Primary alert: fallback_trigger_rate > 0.5% of requests for a route sustained 5m + p95 latency increased > 30% -> severity S2 (investigate automated policy mismatch or infra).
- High severity: host_gpu_mem_util > 92% on >25% of hosts for 3m -> S1 (evacuate / autoscale / failover).
- Silent degradation: rolling eval-score drop > 5% on canary prompts (30m) with no latency change -> S2 (model quality rollback).
- Alert noise control: all alert rules must include route/model filters and not fire for synthetic/canary traffic.

Runbook snippets (links to full runbooks elsewhere):
- If fallback spike + latency spike: check gateway traces for batching anomalies -> examine batch_size distribution, then host queue depth, then scale / roll back recent model rollout.
- If fallback without latency change but eval drop: stop rollout, route traffic to pinned model, trigger quality rollback pipeline.
- If fallback localized to region: check inter-region network metrics, region capacity, and policy routing rules; possibly switch to next region.

Instrumentation TODOs / open questions (action items):
- [ ] Add telemetry.fallback.trigger metric in policy service (ENG-3498)
- [ ] Add lightweight fallback-decision span to policy service trace proto (PR linked above)
- [ ] Revisit sampling ratios: are 1/200 and 1/10 working in prod? Create dashboard to show sampled vs unsampled requests.
- [ ] Define canonical seq_len buckets (suggested: 0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024) for latency slicing.
- [ ] Decide retention for sampled traces tied to SLO windows (30d vs 90d).

Notes / context / quick links:
- This is intentionally pragmatic — avoid creating too many cardinality tags (avoid customer_id on high-card counters). Use customer_tier and route.
- See linked Confluence for fallback policy matrix (linked_artifacts).
- Talk to solutions-eng for customer-specific fallbacks (they have a spreadsheet of 12 customers with special routes).

Appendix: shorthand checklist for first responder:
- Confirm scope: is the incident "fallback" or "quality" or "infra"? Use three checks: fallback_trigger_count, eval_score_change, host_gpu_mem_util.
- Pick mitigation: route->fallback (policy toggle), scale hosts, rollback model, or region failover.
- Record decision in channel #oncall-fallbacks and tag incident id.

End — Lina. Feedback welcome.

Unresolved: what metadata (if any) to attach to fallback_trigger metric to enable customer-level attribution without exploding cardinality? Proposed: include customer_tier + anonymized_customer_bucket (e.g., enterprise/large/other).
